questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Which of the following structures together are referred to as protoplasm?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm and nucleus together are referred to as protoplasm. A cell is surrounded by a cell membrane (or plasma membrane), which encloses a complex material called protoplasm. It consists of a central, denser part called the nucleus, and an outer less dense part called the cytoplasm. The nucleus is surrounded by a nuclear membrane, which encloses chromatin, nucleolus, and nucleoplasm. The cytoplasm consists of cell organelles and cytosol (also called hyaloplasm), which is the liquid component of the cytoplasm present outside the cell organelles. Vacuoplasm refers to the fluid-filled spaces enclosed within membrane-bound cell organelles.

questions.question: What is the cytoplasm present within the channels of the endoplasmic reticulum called?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm that is present within the channels of the endoplasmic reticulum is called vacuoplasm. The presence of the endoplasmic reticulum divides the cytoplasm into two compartments: one within the channels called vacuoplasm and that outside the channels called hyaloplasm or cytosol.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: With respect to the mass ratio, the cell membrane predominantly consists of _______.
questions.explanation: With respect to the mass ratio, the cell membrane predominantly consists of proteins. The mass of proteins either equals or exceeds the mass of lipids in nearly all membranes. Most plasma membranes consist of approximately 50% lipid and 50% protein by weight. The lipid molecules in the cell membrane are predominantly phospholipids. The trilaminar structure of membranes is produced by the arrangement of lipid molecules. Each phospholipid molecule consists of an enlarged head with a phosphate portion and two thin tails. The head end is also called the polar end, while the tail end is the non-polar end. The head end is soluble in water and is said to be hydrophilic. The tail end is insoluble in water and is said to be hydrophobic.

questions.question: Absorption of the fluids into the cell occurs by a process called _______.
questions.explanation: Absorption of fluids into the cell occurs by pinocytosis; the vesicles involved are called pinocytotic vesicles. Endocytosis is a process in which large molecules enter cells by invagination and formation of a vesicle. Some cells use endocytosis to engulf foreign matter such as bacteria; this is phagocytosis. The process of releasing molecules produced within the cytoplasm to the exterior is called exocytosis or reverse pinocytosis.

questions.question: The structure marked with the asterisk in the electron micrograph indicates _____________.
questions.explanation: The structure marked with the asterisk in the electron micrograph indicates presynaptic secretory vesicles. The structure marked with the arrowhead is postsynaptic density. Secretory vesicles are synthesized by neurons and are involved in electrochemical signalling in the brain and neuromuscular junctions. On electron microscopy, mitochondria appear as round or elliptical bodies with outer and inner mitochondrial membranes, cristae, and mitochondrial matrix. Golgi bodies appear as stacks of flattened membranous cisternae surrounded by clusters of vesicles. Ribosomes may be attached to the membrane of rough endoplasmic reticulum or may exist as monosomes or chains of granular structures called polyribosomes associated with mRNA.

questions.question: Which of the following chromatins in the nucleus has a loose appearance and stains lightly with hematoxylin and eosin?
questions.explanation: Euchromatin in the nucleus has a loose appearance and stains lightly with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). On H&E staining, the nucleus stains dark purple or blue while the cytoplasm usually stains pink. In some cells, nuclei are relatively large and stain lightly because of a delicate network of fibers called chromatin. Irregular dark masses are heterochromatin; areas where the network is loose and stains lightly are euchromatin.

questions.question: The lumen of the rough endoplasmic reticulum is continuous with _____.
questions.explanation: The lumen of the rough endoplasmic reticulum is continuous with the perinuclear space. Rough endoplasmic reticulum arises from the outer nuclear membrane; therefore its lumen is continuous with the perinuclear space between the inner and outer nuclear membranes. The lumen is also continuous with the lumen of smooth ER. The ER is a network of flattened membrane-bound structures called cisternae and is classified as rough or smooth according to the presence or absence of attached ribosomes.

questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Which of the following is not a unilayered epithelia?
questions.explanation: Seminiferous epithelium is a complex stratified epithelium consisting of cells that form the lineage of spermatozoa (spermatogonia, spermatocytes and spermatids) together with Sertoli cells. Simple epithelia and pseudostratified epithelium are both unilayered epithelia. Simple epithelium is typically present at sites of absorption, secretion and filtration and, depending on cell shape, is classified as squamous, cuboidal or columnar. Pseudostratified epithelium comprises only a single layer of cells but the nuclei lie at different levels, creating an appearance suggestive of stratification; the trachea is illustrated as an example.

questions.question: What type of epithelium lines the parietal peritoneum?
questions.explanation: The parietal peritoneum is lined by simple squamous epithelium. Simple squamous epithelium is seen in alveoli of lungs, the thin segment of the loop of Henle, blood and lymphatic vessels (endothelium), body cavities such as pleura, peritoneum and pericardium (mesothelium), and the inside of the heart (endocardium).

questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: The thyroid follicles are lined by _____ epithelium.
questions.explanation: Thyroid follicles are lined by cuboidal epithelium. Cuboidal epithelium consists of a single layer of cells in which cell height is approximately equal to cell width, with usually rounded nuclei. Cuboidal cells are seen in thyroid follicles, the surface of the ovary (germinal epithelium), choroid plexuses, the inner surface of the lens, the pigment cell layer of the retina, and proximal convoluted tubules of the kidneys (brush-border cuboidal epithelium).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes the multilayered epithelium that consists of deeper columnar cells and a surface layer of flat cells?
questions.explanation: The multilayered epithelium that consists of deeper columnar cells and a surface layer of flat cells is stratified squamous epithelium. Stratified epithelia include stratified squamous, stratified cuboidal/columnar, and transitional epithelium. In stratified squamous epithelium the deepest layer is columnar, above which are layers of cuboidal cells; toward the surface the cells become increasingly flattened. It may be keratinized or non-keratinized. Stratified cuboidal/columnar epithelium consists of two or more layers of cuboidal or columnar cells respectively; salivary-gland ducts are illustrated. Transitional epithelium is a specialized epithelium lining most of the urinary tract (urothelium). Its deepest layer is columnar or cuboidal, middle cells are polyhedral or pear-shaped, and surface cells are large polypoid/dome/umbrella-shaped cells that flatten on stretching. This apparent transition gives the epithelium its name.

questions.question: The cornea is lined by ________ epithelium.

questions.question: The type of epithelium as shown in the image below is present in _______.
questions.explanation: The epithelium shown is transitional epithelium and is present in the urinary bladder. Transitional epithelium is specialized epithelium lining most of the urinary tract and is also called urothelium. Its deepest layer consists of columnar or cuboidal cells, the middle layer of polyhedral or pear-shaped cells, and the surface layer of large polypoid, dome-shaped or umbrella-shaped cells. On stretching to accommodate urine, the surface cells flatten. It is present in collecting ducts, renal pelvis and calyces, ureter, urinary bladder, and the pre-prostatic and prostatic parts of the urethra.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Microvilli are absent in _______.
questions.explanation: Microvilli are absent in collecting ducts, which are lined by simple columnar epithelium without microvilli. Simple cuboidal or columnar epithelium may show specializations. Microvilli are long finger-like projections that increase absorptive surface area; regularly arranged long microvilli create a striated appearance, whereas irregular arrangement creates a brush border. They are present in small intestine (striated microvilli), gall bladder (brush-border microvilli), and proximal convoluted tubule (brush-border microvilli). Stereocilia are long, branching, non-motile microvilli (stereovilli), found in epididymis and cochlear/vestibular receptor cells. Cilia are hair-like projections concerned with movement and occur in the respiratory tract except lower pharynx and vocal folds, tympanic cavity and auditory tube, uterine tube, and efferent ductules of testis. Columnar cells may also be specialized for secretion, as in mucin-secreting and chief cells of gastric epithelium.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Which of the following is a holocrine gland?
questions.explanation: The sebaceous gland is a holocrine gland. Exocrine glands are classified by mode of secretion. Merocrine (eccrine/epicrine) glands release secretion by exocytosis while the cell remains intact; examples include eccrine sweat glands, salivary glands, exocrine pancreas, and secretion of milk protein casein by mammary glands. Holocrine glands discharge secretion by disintegration of the entire cell, as in sebaceous glands. In apocrine glands the apical part of the cell is shed to discharge secretion; examples include sweat glands in axilla and anogenital regions and secretion of milk fat by mammary glands.

options.text: Tall cells with flat nucleus at base

questions.question: Which of the following fibers of the connective tissue are stained black with silver impregnation?
questions.explanation: Reticular fibers are stained black with the silver impregnation method. They are also called argentophil fibers because of their affinity for silver salts. The three main connective-tissue fiber types are collagen, reticular and elastic fibers. questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the cells present in brown adipose tissue?

options.text: They are larger than in typical adipose tissue.
The fat in the cytoplasm occurs as single locule.
The cytoplasm and nucleus are pushed to periphery.

questions.explanation: The cytoplasm of cells of brown adipose tissue contains numerous mitochondria. Adipose tissue is mainly of two types: yellow/white adipose tissue and brown adipose tissue (embryonic type). White adipose tissue is seen in adults, has larger cells with a single fat droplet, is also called unilocular adipose tissue, has cytoplasm and nucleus pushed to the periphery, and has few mitochondria. Brown adipose tissue is seen in newborns, has smaller cells with multiple fat droplets, is also called multilocular adipose tissue, has cytoplasm and nucleus not pushed to the periphery, and has numerous mitochondria.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.chapter: Cell Structure, Epithelia, Glands & Connective Tissue
questions.question: Reticular fibres are not present in which of the following structures?
questions.explanation: Reticular fibres are not present in the thymus. Reticular fibres are fine, anastomosing fibres composed mainly of type III collagen. They differ from type I collagen in that they are finer and arranged in the form of a network (reticulum). They appear black with silver impregnation and, due to affinity for silver salts, are also known as argentophil fibres. Reticular fibres are mainly found in lymphoid organs such as spleen, lymph node and bone marrow (except thymus), glands, liver and kidneys, basement membrane of epithelia, smooth muscle and nerve cells.
